segments.t: Back at the agency, Gabriel is keeping the promise he made at the end of the last episode: he has taken on receptionist Sofia as a client. Between phone calls at the front desk, Sofia shows him her new professional headshots. We'll hear it in French first; just listen to the tone of their voices.
ASK, bonjour. Oui, je vous la passe.
Gabriel! Voilà mes nouvelles photos.
Elles sont en noir et blanc.
Tu crois qu'elles sont bien?
Oui, très bien. Tes photos sont bonnes.
Vraiment?
Tu es photogénique.
J'aime le regard dans les yeux, et le sourire aussi.
Enfin, vous êtes belle.
C'est simple et naturel.
Vous avez de la grâce. Oui, c'est ça, de la grâce.
Merci, Gabriel!
Bon, au travail!
Et après Sofia, tu prends aussi la fille de la boulangerie?
Elle fera la couverture d'un grand magazine!
Tu l'aimes bien, non?
Jamais avec mes clientes!
Let's go through it line by line. Sofia is answering the agency phone at the reception desk as Gabriel walks in.
ASK, bonjour. Oui, je vous la passe.
'ASK, hello. Yes, I'll put you through to her.' Literally 'I pass her to you', with both short words stacked right before the action word.
Gabriel! Voilà mes nouvelles photos.
'Gabriel! Here are my new photos.' The word for 'new' is in its feminine plural form to match 'photos', and stands before the noun.
Elles sont en noir et blanc.
'They're in black and white.' The word for 'they' is the feminine plural form because it refers to the photos. The colour words here describe the kind of image, rather than the photos themselves.
Tu crois qu'elles sont bien?
'Do you think they're good?' The question keeps ordinary statement order. The rising voice and question mark turn 'you think' into 'do you think'.
Oui, très bien. Tes photos sont bonnes.
'Yes, very good. Your photos are good.' Hear the softer ending on the word for 'good': the written extra letters match the feminine plural word for photos.
Vraiment?
'Really?' One word, asking if he truly means it.
Tu es photogénique.
'You're photogenic.' This describing word has the same form for a man or a woman. Gabriel is saying that Sofia looks good on camera.
J'aime le regard dans les yeux, et le sourire aussi.
'I like the look in your eyes, and the smile too.' French uses 'the eyes' where English says 'your eyes'.
Enfin, vous êtes belle.
'Well, you're beautiful.' Notice how Gabriel suddenly switches from the casual 'you' back to the polite 'you': paying her a compliment makes him shy.
C'est simple et naturel.
'It's simple and natural.' Both adjectives stay in the masculine singular after 'it is'.
Vous avez de la grâce. Oui, c'est ça, de la grâce.
'You have grace. Yes, that's it, grace.' The two words before 'grace' mean 'some', used before an abstract quality.
Merci, Gabriel!
'Thank you, Gabriel!' Sofia is glowing as the lift doors open.
Bon, au travail!
'Right, back to work!' Literally 'to the work'. Gabriel hurries into the lift, where Andréa is waiting.
Et après Sofia, tu prends aussi la fille de la boulangerie?
'And after Sofia, are you taking on the girl from the bakery too?' The action word normally means 'take'. For an agent, taking someone means adding them as a client.
Elle fera la couverture d'un grand magazine!
'She'll be on the cover of a big magazine!' Literally 'she will make the cover', using the future tense of 'to make'.
Tu l'aimes bien, non?
'You like her, don't you?' Adding the word meaning 'well' after 'love' makes the everyday expression for liking someone. The final 'no?' asks him to confirm Andréa's suspicion.
Jamais avec mes clientes!

'Never with my clients!' The final word has a feminine ending because he means female clients. Its spoken ending differs from the masculine form: listen for the clear final consonant. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more.
ASK, bonjour. Oui, je vous la passe.
Gabriel! Voilà mes nouvelles photos.
Elles sont en noir et blanc.
Tu crois qu'elles sont bien?
Oui, très bien. Tes photos sont bonnes.
Vraiment?
Tu es photogénique.
J'aime le regard dans les yeux, et le sourire aussi.
Enfin, vous êtes belle.
C'est simple et naturel.
Vous avez de la grâce. Oui, c'est ça, de la grâce.
Merci, Gabriel!
Bon, au travail!
Et après Sofia, tu prends aussi la fille de la boulangerie?
Elle fera la couverture d'un grand magazine!
Tu l'aimes bien, non?
Jamais avec mes clientes!

As they step out of the lift into the corridor, tax inspector Colette Brancillon politely reminds them about the documents she asked for, and Gabriel and Andréa worry that tax inspectors always find something wrong. See you next time!
À demain!
